prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active peptide form that made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B041 prize for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. After reading the full first-round exchange, the case still rests on the discovery chain and not on the six first-place openings. Holst established incretin secretion and action in humans, Drucker defined proglucagon-derived peptide biology and its actions, and Mojsov identified the bioactive truncated GLP-1 form, which is the step that turned a hormone into a drug target. That chain led to agonists with large, independently confirmed benefit in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The mechanism is settled and the recognition is neither premature nor late. A prize for the principle and the active molecule matches the idea that the award goes to a specific discovery that changed a field, and it fits within three names without displacing a discoverer.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point, and round 1 did not remove it. Habener sits outside the credited names, Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is described as contested by every member, and none of us can adjudicate it from the permitted files. Leaving out Knudsen means the citation honours the hormone and the active peptide while the drugs that reached patients rest on a step the prize does not name. I weigh this as a real cost, but not as a reason to put a developer in place of a discoverer. If the committee had verified evidence that Mojsov's claim fails, my configuration would be wrong in one name and I would reopen it. I also note that the argument against Knudsen carries less weight if the citation is read broadly, so I would keep the wording tied to discovery and not claim more than the three names support.

responses.point: Sandberg moved from Knudsen to the Mojsov trio but still calls Knudsen's acylated long-acting analogue programme a distinct achievement and not a later detail, and says the citation can carry the drug history.
responses.response: I accept that Knudsen's step is distinct, and I do not call it a detail, since without semaglutide and liraglutide there is no obesity indication. But distinct is not the same as discovery. The chair's question is whether wording can honour the analogues without naming her, and I think it can only go so far. The phrase 'made incretin-based treatment possible' in my citation recognises that the discovery enabled therapy, but a citation that praised the long-acting analogue programme while naming three others would invite the very criticism you describe. I would keep the citation to hormone and active peptide, and leave the analogue programme to a possible later prize built on its own claim. This shifts only slightly from round 1, where I was prepared to accept the review of Mojsov and Habener. If that review is not possible, I still prefer Mojsov to Knudsen on the information in front of us.

responses.point: Svenningsson, as chair, asks which alternative is next and what condition it needs, and he ranked B011 second and B023 only eighth, citing the unresolved credit of Eshhar and Gross and the judgement on Rosenberg.
responses.response: I have moved my order of alternatives. In round 1 I listed B011 first and B023 second. I now list B023 first. Linnarsson's argument that a new therapeutic modality with durable remissions is what this prize rewards persuaded me, and I think my own concern about the clinical gap for B011 applies with force when the chair himself puts B011 second because of its clean attribution. On your point about B023 I still hold that Rosenberg belongs to a separate lineage of adoptive cell transfer, and that June and Sadelain alone are the defensible engineering pair. The main condition for B023 is to decide how to treat Eshhar's chimeric-receptor concept. If the committee cannot name him, I would want the citation limited to clinically validated CAR-T design and not claim the original idea. B011 would need a demonstrated therapeutic derivative before I would put it first.

responses.point: Linnarsson would swap Knudsen for Mojsov rather than add a fourth name, and in round 1 he asked whether the weak disease link of B011 weighs against a modality like B023 with demonstrated remissions.
responses.response: I agree that a fourth name is not an option, and I would not want the committee to try to square this by stretching the rule. On the substance of your swap, I think the discovery question comes first: if the committee decides that the prize should honour the drug, then Knudsen would have to replace Mojsov, since Drucker and Holst are the physiology. I do not take that view, and my reason is that the identification of GLP-1(7-36) is a discovery of what the active molecule is, which stands whatever drug followed. I take your point on B011 and accept that my round-1 ranking of it as a clean mechanism does not answer the medical question. On that point you have moved me to put B023 above it in my alternatives.

responses.point: El-Manira holds that a basic cell-biology prize like B011 is easier to defer than B041, and that the credit for B023 is less settled than for B041 because Eshhar is outside the credited names.
responses.response: I agree on both points and they shape my final order. B011 has the cleanest attribution of the shortlist, but you are right that its impact on patients is indirect, and deferral costs less than for B041. For B023 I accept your point that June, Sadelain and Rosenberg are three different contributions and that credit is less settled than for GLP-1. I would not use B023 as a lead this year for that reason, but I would use it as the better alternative if the GLP-1 allocation breaks down. Where I differ from you is on how much the Mojsov priority dispute should count. You say you would not drop her without evidence that the claim fails. I agree, and I would add that the absence of the evidence in our permitted files cuts both ways, so it cannot be a reason to remove her either.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius keeps B044 and B023 as her next cases because both created a therapeutic modality, and she regards B011 as a credible later or companion candidate and not a front-runner.
responses.response: Your argument that the medical dimension should count heavily is the one that moved my alternatives. I accept that B011, however clean, cannot displace a discovery with demonstrated benefit. On B044, I still think the pair is clean, but I hold my round-1 view that it risks rewarding the first of many cytokine-targeted drugs, and I do not put it among my two alternatives. We differ on B044 versus B011 as a second choice, and I do not think support counts should settle it. I also take your point that the priority record needs checking before the vote, and I share it.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide and Habener's claim would change the third name if the record could be checked. I cannot settle this from the permitted files and I do not claim to.
Whether the committee can draft a citation that honours the discovery and enabled therapy without implying credit for the long-acting analogue programme that is not named.
Whether B023 can be given a defensible laureate set with Eshhar and Gross outside the credited names, and whether the checkpoint-inhibitor prize makes CAR-T early, which I do not think it does.
How much weight the committee should give to demonstrated patient benefit versus mechanism, which decides the order of B023 and B011.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict that requires recusal. I disclose my nuclear-receptor collaboration with Ronald Evans at the Salk Institute and my work with Johan Ericson, none of whom is credited on the shortlist. I also note my roughly twenty co-authored works with Per Svenningsson and one 2009 paper with Abdel El Manira, which concern neuroscience topics and do not involve a shortlisted ballot or credited name. Shared Karolinska affiliation with colleagues does not affect my judgement of B041, B023 or B011.
